subject: Week 22: build the 6-month visit list - iron screen is universal
bodyText:
This week
Days 152-158 widen the social world: he knows familiar people, studies himself in the mirror, blows raspberries, and takes turns making sounds - a CDC 6-month checkpoint. Tripod sitting is emerging for some; the CDC sits-without-support checkpoint is 9 months, so propped is still the expected posture. His sharpening preference for the two of you is the precursor to stranger anxiety, which peaks at 7-10 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Increased clinginess and protest at being put down - attachment sharpening, on schedule.
- [monitor] Little interest in toys, minimal vocalizing, or scarce eye contact - document and raise at the 6-month visit.
- [monitor] Night wakings still at 4+ after six or more weeks of consistent response - see the sleep re-evaluation below.
- [call within 24h] New ear-pulling with fever, or illness symptoms persisting past 48 hours - same-day call.
- [call now] Seizure-like activity, fever of 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, labored breathing, or blue lips - call 911, don't second-guess.

Enrichment opportunities
- Stock the solids shelf: iron-fortified single-grain oat cereal (the standard starting point) plus the week-one produce - avocado, banana, sweet potato. If baby-led weaning won the method decision, skip spoons and plan soft strips; if purees, a NumNum-style pre-loaded spoon. AAP - Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Point and name consistently during read-alouds - this is a cat; the cat is on the mat. Conversational turns, not raw word count, are what predict language outcomes in the neuroimaging data. Romeo et al. 2018 (PubMed): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Get on the floor at his eye level after sitting him up - lie down beside him rather than looming above. Eye-level interaction raises the quality of vocal turn-taking.
- Re-evaluate the sleep plan if you rode out the regression: past week 22 with 4+ nightly wakings, pick a formal method and commit for seven nights. Graduated extinction shows meaningful improvement by night 5-7, with no measurable harm to behavior or attachment at 5-year follow-up (Hiscock 2012). AAP - Getting Your Baby to Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Register with Stanford SVNDL this week if the baby-lab batch never happened - the 3-6-month eligibility ceiling closes around day 180, four weeks out. Stanford SVNDL: https://svndl.stanford.edu/participate/

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26-Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit - bring the list above. Vaccines: RV #3 (if RV5), DTaP #3, Hib #3 (if PRP-T), PCV #3, influenza #1; iron/hemoglobin screen; solids-readiness assessment.
- Day 166-172 (week of Oct 24, 2026): solids could start this week if the visit lands at the front of the window - shelf stocked per above.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Supports whole weight on legs when held standing
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Builds leg strength for eventual pulling-to-stand. Does not need to bear weight independently.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/supports-weight-on-legs/complete

- Moves things from one hand to the other
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Bilateral coordination across the midline. Often accompanied by mouthing the transferred object.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/transfers-objects-hand-to-hand/complete

- Closes lips to show she doesn't want more food
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Pre-verbal refusal. Important to respect — supports developing satiety cues.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/closes-lips-not-more/complete

- Enjoys back-and-forth social play
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Active turn-taking in physical or vocal games. Distinct from earlier passive enjoyment of stimulation.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/enjoys-social-play/complete

- Sits without support
  AAP window: day 150-270
  What to look for: Hands free for play. WHO motor study cites 3.8-9.2 mo as the typical range.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-without-support/complete
